original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum. Report the word's packing cap from ceiling.ceiling() and the fraction of it realized; label packing gains as such.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

actual_scope: Review-and-compose of the two open T16 owner-map PRs on the selected PR1094 supplier (PR1407, PR2077), a bounded two-stage ejection-cycle search on PR1407's map (the first version of this package), then a longer finite search on that map (depth-8 ejection cycles alternated with CP-SAT large-neighbourhood re-assignments) and a min-diff re-assignment toward the selected map at the same idle profile. Widths, call order, windows and both suppliers are unchanged; only owner fields of whole helper roles change.
scope_change_reason: Self-selected, not drawn by scripts/choose_research_task.py: the session started as a review of PR1407 and PR2077 and whether their moves compose (they do not: every PR2077 subset is illegal on PR1407's map). The closest catalogue card is selected-packing. The search started from an unmerged PR's map (PR1407), but the shipped map is stated and verified only against the merged selected PR1094 map; PR1407 is lineage and credit, not a dependency.
bottleneck_link: Strictly decreases the complete complex moment of the binding complex supplier while preserving rank mass 1041408, deficit 5120, the local gauge44 supplier and the 144-call chronology.
stop_rule: kappa search: stop when the session's search budget ended (gains were still coming; no stall criterion was met). Min-diff: stop when the global two-fill MIP reached its time limit or proved optimality, followed by the strict replay, the independent seed67 audit and pricing at the unchanged idle profile.
evidence: Unchanged PR1087 strict T16 replay passes all 11 stages with controls 69/12/6/15, actual_73column_sigmas 10000, kappa 0.001672702955495933 (conservative 0.001672702952644): +2.5563e-5 relative over the selected record, +2.214e-8 over PR1407 and +1.845e-8 over this package's first version. Seed67 auditor R1-R7, X1, X2 and its 11 controls pass; pinned-engine pricing and the PR1069 sweep agree. The map differs from the selected PR1094 map in 70 rows (55 relocated helpers, 15 offset-only). Conditional on the selected PR1094 inherited assumptions; no open-PR dependency.
author: Philippe Van Velzen
ai_assistance: Substantial Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance: PR review, composition test, search implementation, min-diff re-assignment, replay and packaging. No independent human review claimed.

open_questions.question: How much further does the finite LNS go on this supplier's T16 owner packing?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The search was stopped while still improving (its last 45-minute run still added +3.85e-9); it is not an optimum.
open_questions.first_step: Run search/loop3.sh from data/OWNERS.json.gz under a memory cap and strict-replay each new best, then rerun the min-diff step.
open_questions.blocked_by: Compute time; random plateau moves make the raw search output hard to review, so each result needs the min-diff step again.

open_questions.question: What is the best attainable idle-residual profile for the selected supplier's T16 windows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A certified relaxation bound would show how much kappa remains in owner packing at all, and whether continuing the LNS is worthwhile.
open_questions.first_step: Solve a bin-level LP or Lagrangian relaxation over (owner, child, port) bins with the family-per-call constraint and the concave per-residual cost.
open_questions.blocked_by: No certified relaxation for the joint family/time constraints exists yet.

open_questions.question: Is the relocation count of the min-diff map minimal for this idle profile?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Smaller diffs are cheaper to review; the shipped map is a MIP/LNS result, not a proven minimum (the two-fill model's dual bound is 92 relocations, but the any-fill LNS went below it to 55).
open_questions.first_step: Run more rounds of search/mindiff_lns2.py from the shipped map with larger neighbourhoods and longer sub-MIP limits, or solve the any-fill model on the remaining region exactly.
open_questions.blocked_by: The any-fill model has a weak LP relaxation; HiGHS found no incumbent in 400 s globally without a warm start, so no useful lower bound is known.
